method: Additional semantic-topic search of current canonical439 visible stem/choices, then lexical ranking within topic; actual candidate text read, no keys/audits

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is behind on continuing education for the current calendar year. She attends an intensive live conference held on a single day in December and the authorized provider issues her a statement of credit for 12 contact hours earned that day. She wants to apply all 12 to that calendar year. How many of those contact hours may she apply?

choices.text: The full 12, because the daily restriction applies to home study rather than live programs.
The full 12, because live conference programming carries no daily restriction.
Ten, because a registrant may not exceed ten contact hours in a calendar day.
None, because contact hours earned in December are credited to the following cycle.
Eight, because a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours in a calendar day.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired 61 days ago. It has never been suspended or revoked. The pharmacist pays the renewal and late fees this morning and asks to begin a shift while the Board processes the renewal. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The pharmacist falls within the 60-day fee-only branch and may practice once payment is submitted.
Any lapse beyond 60 days automatically requires passage of the MPJE before renewal.
Direct oversight by another pharmacist permits practice until the registration is renewed.
Board conditions may apply, but the over-two-year MPJE branch does not; practice must wait for renewal.
The registration remains effective for six months after expiration if all continuing education was completed on time.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee working under the direct supervision of a pharmacist is asked to answer the pharmacy telephone during a staffing crunch and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The trainee may take the prescription while under direct supervision.
The trainee may take the prescription if the pharmacist listens on a second handset.
The trainee may take the prescription if it is for a Schedule VI drug.
The trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
The trainee may take the prescription after 500 hours of trainee employment.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.
A lapse exceeding two years permanently bars renewal of the technician license.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription for generic buprenorphine sublingual tablets for opioid use disorder with a 90-day quantity. Which quantity rule should the pharmacist apply?

choices.text: A 30-day ceiling applies to every Schedule III opioid.
Every Schedule III prescription permits a 90-day fill.
The initial-opiate seven-day limit controls OUD treatment.
The OUD pathway may permit one fill of up to 90 days.
Five refills may be combined into one 90-day fill.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a 90-day Depo-Testosterone prescription with two refills. Which statements should the pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A non-opioid Schedule III drug may qualify for a 90-day single fill.
Each covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
Any refills remain subject to federal count and time limits.
Hormone therapy makes the product Schedule VI.
A 90-day fill removes federal refill restrictions.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially fills a Schedule II prescription at the patient's request two days after the prescription was issued. On day 29 after issuance, the patient asks a different pharmacy to dispense the balance because the first pharmacy is closed. On day 31, the patient returns to the first pharmacy for the balance. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The second pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 29 because the federal 30-day period has not expired.
The first pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 31 because the 30 days run from the initial partial fill.
Either pharmacy may dispense the balance if it can access the original prescription electronically.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted: only the pharmacy that made the partial fill may dispense the balance, and it must do so no later than 30 days after issuance.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted because every Schedule II remainder is due within 72 hours of the partial fill.

visible_originals.stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is asked about a dispensing from last year. Its records contain no entry that the patient failed to accept the pharmacist's offer to counsel, and no entry that counselling was actually given. What follows from that state of the records?

choices.text: Nothing follows; the records are simply silent about what happened that day.
A presumption arises that the counselling was provided to that patient.
A presumption arises that the counselling was not provided to that patient.
The pharmacy must instead produce the dispensing pharmacist's recollection.
The pharmacy is in breach, because counselling must be affirmatively recorded.

visible_originals.stem: A hospice patient needs a Schedule II narcotic. The prescriber faxes a valid prescription to the pharmacy and clearly indicates on the prescription that the patient is a hospice patient. What is the federal consequence of those facts?

choices.text: The fax may serve as the original Schedule II prescription under the hospice narcotic exception.
The fax is an original only if the patient also resides in an LTCF.
Hospice status permits refills on the Schedule II prescription.
The pharmacy must wait for a paper original before dispensing in every hospice case.
The notation is irrelevant because hospice exceptions apply only to Schedule III-V drugs.

visible_originals.stem: A retail pharmacy has expired oxycodone tablets in its own registered inventory. Which statements correctly describe federal disposal pathways and documentation? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy may transfer controlled substances to a DEA-registered reverse distributor while following applicable transfer, inventory, ordering, and record requirements.
If the pharmacy itself destroys controlled substances, leaving intact tablets in an ordinary trash bag satisfies the federal destruction standard.
Registrant destruction must render the controlled substances non-retrievable.
DEA Form 106 is the routine destruction record for expired stock.
When a registrant destroys or causes destruction, the required destruction record is generally documented using DEA Form 41 with the required details.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is counseling a patient on a new inhaled therapy. Which items does the regulation identify as information counseling may include? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy's wholesale acquisition cost for the medication.
Special directions and instructions for preparation, administration and use by the patient.
Techniques for self-monitoring drug therapy.
Proper storage and disposal of the medication.
Action to be taken in the event of a missed dose or adverse reaction.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy plans to mail a temperature-sensitive prescription using a common carrier. The proposed packaging cannot reasonably maintain the product's labeled storage conditions during the expected transit. What should the pharmacy do?

choices.text: Ship it because use of a common carrier transfers responsibility for product stability to the carrier.
Ship it if the patient agrees to accept the risk of temperature excursion.
Use a packing and transportation method that protects medication integrity and stability before sending the prescription.
Remove the labeled storage directions so the carrier is not responsible for them.
Convert the order to an in-store pickup without telling the patient.
